name: solidvents-mcp

tools.name: list_patterns
tools.description: The SolidVents pattern types — ids array (a grid), random, spiral, concentric, fibonacci (sunflower), cross_lines, path, voronoi, flow_lines, and ai_custom (your own arrangement rule, for when no built-in can place the holes) — with when to use each, plus the design guide. Start here — the guide it returns is the method for matching a user's picture (measure → find the repeat unit → layers → gradients → compare). All SolidVents tools require a Pro account.

tools.name: get_pattern_schema
tools.description: Parameters (with units, ranges, defaults) for one pattern type, plus the shared hole / boundary / noise / STEP parameters and how gradients work. Call before preview_design.

tools.name: list_recipes
tools.description: Search 141 ready-made recipes (every SolidVents marketplace preset, translated into this server's parameters) by technique tags and/or a look query. Returns the best matches with a one-line look description, technique summary, thumbnail URL, and one image of their thumbnails. Use it as a DICTIONARY: after you have analysed the user's picture (measured pitch, found the repeat unit, decided which layers / gradients it needs — see list_patterns guide), look up how a technique is parametrised here and copy the mechanism, keeping your own measurements. Do not pick the closest-looking preset and tweak it — the result then looks like that preset, not like the user's picture.

query.description: What it looks like, in plain English: motif, arrangement, how it changes across the panel. E.g. "square tiles with a quarter-circle bite that grows", "hexagon rings getting thicker", "wavy flow lines", "halftone photo".

tags.description: Only recipes having all these technique tags (prefix ok), e.g. ["layer:subtract"], ["pattern:flow_lines"], ["gradient:angle"]. Call with no arguments to see the tag list.

thumbnails.description: Default true: include one image showing the matches' thumbnails left→right, top→bottom in result order (4 per row)

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.description: Returns parameters (design, hole_shape, gradients, path_shape, boundary_shape, reference_image) that reproduce a marketplace preset exactly when passed to preview_design / export_design / open_in_app, plus what each part does and the preset thumbnail. Use it to see how a technique is parametrised (layer structure, gradient settings) and copy the mechanism with your own measurements — not as a look-alike to tweak.

thumbnail.description: Default true: include the preset thumbnail image

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: Community presets from the SolidVents marketplace (name + thumbnail URL). Use load_preset to get one as a starting design.

tools.name: load_preset
tools.description: Returns the full design of a marketplace preset (e.g. "#001"). Pass it (optionally edited) as `design` to preview_design / export_design.

tools.name: preview_design
tools.description: Generate the pattern and return a PNG preview plus stats (hole count, canvas size). With compare {url|data_base64} it returns reference | design | overlay side by side plus overlap numbers — use that on every round when matching a picture of a PATTERN. With mockup {url|data_base64, corners} it composites the design onto the user's photo of the OBJECT the pattern is for (perspective-mapped onto the corners you give) and returns that picture plus a link — use it to show the user the finished design in place. Deterministic for the same seed.

design.description: SolidVents design parameters: { pattern, ...keys from get_pattern_schema }. A full state from load_preset or an exported SVG also works.

svg.description: A SolidVents-exported SVG (its embedded state is used as the design; `design` keys override it).

gradients.description: Simplified gradient controllers; see get_pattern_schema → gradients. Appended to any controllers already in `design`.

fill.description: loop only. Default true = the whole interior is at target; false = only a band of radius on each side of the loop line (e.g. an outer ring of smaller holes)

curve.description: line/loop: smooth curve through the points instead of straight segments

corner_radius.description: line/loop without curve: round the corners (mm)

single_side.description: line/loop: affect only one side of the path

symmetric.description: angle: opposite angle on each side of the line

dropout.description: size: randomly remove this % of holes inside the range

repeat.description: Tile this controller across the whole canvas — for rhythms that repeat (clusters of big holes on a lattice, pulsing bands)

stagger.description: Shift every other row by dx/2

hole_shape.description: Custom hole outline as an SVG path. Use this for chevrons, slots, leaves, logos — anything beyond circle/rectangle/polygon/star. Sets pointShape to custom.

svg_path.description: SVG path data for one hole outline, e.g. "M0 0 L5 3 L10 0 L10 2.5 L5 5.5 L0 2.5 Z" (units arbitrary, y down). Use layers instead for composite holes.

circles.description: Construction outline (arcs + common tangent lines, the way logos are drawn): circles in order around the outline; r > 0 bulge, r < 0 dent, r = 0 corner. Units arbitrary, y down (same as svg_path). Rules and examples: CONSTRUCTION under hole_shape in get_pattern_schema.

r.description: Radius. r > 0: the outline bulges around this circle (convex arc, circle inside the shape); r < 0: the outline dents inward along it (concave arc, circle outside the shape); r = 0: a sharp corner at (x, y)

rect.description: A rectangle w × h centred on (0,0) instead of a path — bars, slats, strips. Place and turn it with transform. fillets rounds its corners

transform.description: Placement of this piece: turned by rotation about its own origin, then moved to (x, y); applied before mirror. Draw the piece around (0,0) and put its position here — no corner arithmetic for slanted bars

mirror.description: For the single outline given by svg_path / circles / rect; in layers each layer has its own. 2 = mirror across x = 0, 3–8 = copies turned about (0, 0); draw the shape once (open half or one repeat) — see SYMMETRY in get_pattern_schema.

layers.description: Composite hole: layers bottom→top with roles (union/subtract) and per-layer gradient behaviour, at most 12. See get_pattern_schema → hole_shape. If a unit needs more than 12 pieces, simplify the motif or make the unit smaller (a bigger repeat with fewer pieces per layer); say so to the user rather than silently dropping pieces.

svg_path.description: SVG path for this layer, same coordinate frame as the other layers. Give svg_path, circles or rect

circles.description: Construction outline (arcs + common tangent lines, the way logos are drawn): circles in order around the outline; r > 0 bulge, r < 0 dent, r = 0 corner. Same coordinate frame as svg_path. Rules and examples: CONSTRUCTION under hole_shape in get_pattern_schema.

role.description: normal = own outline (overlaps XOR), union = merge into layers below, subtract = cut from layers below

gradient.description: Reaction to a size gradient: default scales with the hole, fixed never scales, independent scales about its own pivot

mirror.description: Symmetry about the origin of the path coordinates (the hole centre): 1 = none, 2 = mirror across x = 0, 3–8 = copies turned about (0, 0). Draw a symmetric shape once (an open half, or one repeat) and let mirror complete it. Rules: SYMMETRY under hole_shape in get_pattern_schema.

lock_width.description: independent layer: a size gradient does not change its width

lock_height.description: independent layer: a size gradient does not change its height

frame_rotation.description: independent layer: orientation (deg) of the box its pivot is taken from

fillets.description: Live rounded corners: a number rounds every sharp corner by that radius, or [{corner: anchor index, radius}] (same units as svg_path). Prefer this over drawing arcs by hand

lock_fillet.description: independent layer: corner radius stays the same when a size gradient scales the layer

smooth.description: Clean up an outline traced from a picture: drops jitter below the tolerance (a number in path units; true = 3% of the outline size) and fits a smooth curve through what is left. Bends sharper than 50° stay as corners. Set it whenever you traced a blurry or low-res picture — the result must be cleaner than the picture, not a copy of its noise. Left out: an outline of 8+ straight anchors with mostly shallow bends is smoothed automatically (see warnings); false keeps the exact polygon.

size_mm.description: Size of the hole's larger dimension in mm (default: pointSize)

units.description: fit (default) = centre the outline and scale its larger side to size_mm; cell = use coordinates as given, 1 unit = pointSize mm, (0,0) = hole centre (recipes use this): divide your millimetres by pointSize and keep the coordinates within about ±0.5 (a unit spanning more than 2 units is rescaled, see get_pattern_schema)

lock_width.description: A size gradient leaves the hole width unchanged

lock_height.description: A size gradient leaves the hole height unchanged

smooth.description: Apply smooth (see layers[].smooth) to every layer: true = auto tolerance, number = tolerance in path units

path_shape.description: Pattern "path" only: the guide path(s) holes are placed along (open or closed). Use with pathMode / pathPointCount / pathSpacing / pathCopies.

svg_path.description: SVG path in canvas millimetres: centre (0,0), x right, y down. Give svg_path, circles or rect

circles.description: Construction outline (arcs + common tangent lines, the way logos are drawn): circles in order around the outline; r > 0 bulge, r < 0 dent, r = 0 corner. Canvas millimetres, closed outline. Rules and examples: CONSTRUCTION under hole_shape in get_pattern_schema.

custom_arrangement.description: AI custom arrangement (sets pattern "ai_custom"): your own rule for where the hole centres go, with parameters the user edits in the app. Use it whenever no built-in pattern can place the holes the way the user needs — no need to ask first, but never instead of tuning a built-in that fits. Read get_pattern_schema("ai_custom") first.

name.description: Short name shown above the parameter fields in the app, in the user's language

params.description: The numbers the user can edit in the app, as number fields

key.description: Required. Name used in expressions (letters, digits, _)

term.description: Name from custom_arrangement.terms in get_pattern_schema("ai_custom"), e.g. "ringGap": the app shows it in each viewer's language, so the rule reads right when shared to another country

label.description: Field label: with a term, optional; without one, give all 12 app languages { en, "zh-TW", "zh-CN", ja, ko, de, fr, es, pt, it, tr, th }

default.description: Required. The value the user gets

step.description: Step of the number field (arrow keys / wheel)

unit.description: mm for lengths (scale with the canvas), deg, count (whole numbers), none (ratios, strengths)

body.description: Required. Statements: {"let": {name: expr}}, {"for": "k", "from"?, "to", "step"?, "do": [...]}, {"if": expr, "then": [...], "else"?: [...]}, {"hole": {"x", "z" (or "r", "a"), "rotation"?, "size"?}} — rotation and size go INSIDE hole. Expressions are strings; trig in degrees. Full spec: get_pattern_schema("ai_custom") → custom_arrangement

values.description: Parameter values for this call only (e.g. to test the ends of a range); the defaults stay what the user gets

reference_image.description: Use an image as a controller: its brightness drives hole size / spacing / angle / shape across the canvas (the "reference image" workflow).

url.description: http(s) URL of a PNG or JPEG

path.description: Local file path (local MCP only; must be inside the folder the server was started in, its output folder, or a folder passed with --allow-dir)

data_base64.description: Raw PNG/JPEG bytes as base64 — only when your runtime hands you the real bytes (a file you read programmatically). Never retype a picture you can merely see: it will not decode. For a photo the user pasted into the chat, ask for a URL, or, if you have a code sandbox, call design_geometry and composite there.

preset.description: Use the background image stored in a marketplace preset, e.g. "#082" (get_recipe fills this in; keeps the recipe's imgScale / imgOffX / imgOffY)

mode.description: Which property the image brightness drives

invert.description: true = bright areas get the effect instead of dark

contrast.description: Gamma on the brightness map, 1 = as is

scale.description: mm per image pixel; default fits the image to the canvas

width_px.description: Preview width in pixels (default 768; with compare each of the three panels gets this width, default 512; reference_only default 1024)

zoom_mm.description: Render only a square of this many mm (e.g. 40) to inspect the hole shape and tiling closely — centred on the canvas centre, or on zoom_at. Omit for the whole canvas.

zoom_at.description: Centre of the zoom_mm window in canvas mm [x, z] (default [0, 0]) — look at a corner or at one motif

reference_only.description: true = do not draw the design; return only the reference picture (compare.url/path/data_base64, with its scale/offset/region) fitted to the canvas with a labelled mm grid. Use it FIRST to measure pitch, motif size and where the motifs sit before you draw anything; with zoom_mm / zoom_at to look closely. design still sets the canvas size the picture is fitted to.

compare.description: Compare the preview with the user's reference picture: returns reference | design | overlay side by side plus overlap numbers and the shift that would align them best. Overlay = three-colour diff over the reference: green = matched, red = a hole the picture does not have, blue = an opening you are missing. Purely visual — it does not change the design. Use it on every iteration when matching a picture.

url.description: http(s) URL of the user's reference picture (PNG/JPEG)

path.description: Local file path (local MCP only; must be inside the folder the server was started in, its output folder, or a folder passed with --allow-dir)

data_base64.description: Raw PNG/JPEG bytes as base64 — only when your runtime hands you the real bytes (a file you read programmatically). Never retype a picture you can merely see: it will not decode. For a photo the user pasted into the chat, ask for a URL, or, if you have a code sandbox, call design_geometry and composite there.

layout.description: side_by_side (default) = reference | design | overlay in one PNG; overlay = just the overlay

invert.description: true = the openings in the reference are the BRIGHT parts (backlit panel, a photo of a stone screen against the sky). After setting it, check a zoomed compare: green must land on the openings, not on the bars

scale.description: mm per reference pixel; default fits the picture (or region) to the canvas and centres it (same fit as reference_image)

offset.description: Where the centre of the reference (or of region) lands on the canvas, in mm (x right, y down); default (0, 0). Use it to slide the picture; metrics.suggested_shift tells you how much

region.description: Use only this part of the reference, in reference pixels (top-left x, y and width, height): crop away frames, background, the wall around a photographed panel. The region is what gets fitted / scaled

threshold.description: Grey level (0–255) below which a reference pixel counts as an opening (above, with invert). Default: Otsu, reported as reference_threshold. Set it when shadows or a frame are being counted as openings (reference_dark_area much larger than the real open area)

grid_mm.description: Draw labelled millimetre grid lines every this many mm over the reference and the overlay panels (axes in orange) — to read pitch and positions

measure.description: Also find every opening in the reference (same placement, invert, region and threshold) and return its centre in canvas mm, size, polar position about the pattern centre, plus rings (radius, count, angle step, phase) and rows (z, count, pitch). Use it with reference_only to read the rule behind an arrangement — counts per ring and phases are not readable by eye

mockup.description: Composite the design onto the user's own photo so they see it in place (a mockup). Returns the photo with the pattern perspective-mapped onto the given corners, plus a link to the image when the server can store it. Use it when the user gave a picture of the THING the pattern is for (speaker, cabinet door, façade, car grille…), not a picture of a pattern to copy — that is compare.

url.description: http(s) URL of the user's photo (PNG/JPEG): the product, panel, wall or object the pattern will go on

path.description: Local file path (local MCP only; must be inside the folder the server was started in, its output folder, or a folder passed with --allow-dir)

data_base64.description: Raw PNG/JPEG bytes as base64 — only when your runtime hands you the real bytes (a file you read programmatically). Never retype a picture you can merely see: it will not decode. For a photo the user pasted into the chat, ask for a URL, or, if you have a code sandbox, call design_geometry and composite there.

corners.description: Where the panel is in the photo: its 4 corners in order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. Any quadrilateral — the pattern is perspective-mapped onto it. Default units: fractions 0–1 of the photo width/height. Omit to cover the whole photo.

region.description: Axis-aligned alternative to corners: top-left x,y and width,height (same units). Ignored when corners is given.

units.description: fraction (default) = 0–1 of the photo size; px = photo pixels (the response tells you the photo size)

hole_color.description: Colour painted into the holes, hex. Default #141414 (dark = you see the shadowed inside through the holes). Use a light colour for a backlit panel.

outline.description: Draw a cyan outline around the region, to check the corners before the final render

output_px.description: Width in pixels of the stored full-size mockup (default and max 2048; the photo is downscaled to this). The picture returned inline in the result is a 1024-px preview for checking placement; image_url is the full-size JPEG. Lower this only to speed up iteration rounds.

tools.name: design_geometry
tools.description: Returns the design's hole outlines as flattened polygons in millimetres — the same layout the app exports, compacted (each distinct shape once, then [x, y, shape, scale, rotation] per hole) — plus a Python (Pillow + numpy) recipe that composites them onto a photo with perspective. Use it when the user pasted a photo of their OBJECT straight into the chat and you have a code sandbox: the photo is in your sandbox but cannot reach this server, so bring the design to the photo. Save the first text block verbatim as design.json, put the recipe in a .py file with PHOTO and CORNERS set, run it, hand the user the output file. Prefer preview_design.mockup when the photo has a URL. Deterministic for the same seed. NOT for CAD: curves are flattened into short straight segments and coordinates are rounded — good enough to draw on a photo, not to machine. If the user wants the geometry in CAD (Creo, SolidWorks, Fusion…) or a cutting file, that is a file request: use export_design (STEP for 3D CAD, DXF or SVG for 2D).

r.description: Radius. r > 0: the outline bulges around this circle (convex arc, circle inside the shape); r < 0: the outline dents inward along it (concave arc, circle outside the shape); r = 0: a sharp corner at (x, y)

rect.description: A rectangle w × h centred on (0,0) instead of a path — bars, slats, strips. Place and turn it with transform. fillets rounds its corners

transform.description: Placement of this piece: turned by rotation about its own origin, then moved to (x, y); applied before mirror. Draw the piece around (0,0) and put its position here — no corner arithmetic for slanted bars

mirror.description: Symmetry about the canvas centre: 1 = none, 2 = mirror across x = 0, 3–8 = copies turned about (0, 0). Draw a symmetric shape once (an open half, or one repeat) and let mirror complete it. Rules: SYMMETRY under hole_shape in get_pattern_schema.

smooth.description: Clean up a path traced from a picture: drops jitter below the tolerance (mm; true = 3% of the path size) and fits a smooth curve; bends sharper than 50° stay sharp.

custom_arrangement.description: AI custom arrangement (sets pattern "ai_custom"): your own rule for where the hole centres go, with parameters the user edits in the app. Use it whenever no built-in pattern can place the holes the way the user needs — no need to ask first, but never instead of tuning a built-in that fits. Read get_pattern_schema("ai_custom") first.

name.description: Short name shown above the parameter fields in the app, in the user's language

params.description: The numbers the user can edit in the app, as number fields

key.description: Required. Name used in expressions (letters, digits, _)

term.description: Name from custom_arrangement.terms in get_pattern_schema("ai_custom"), e.g. "ringGap": the app shows it in each viewer's language, so the rule reads right when shared to another country

label.description: Field label: with a term, optional; without one, give all 12 app languages { en, "zh-TW", "zh-CN", ja, ko, de, fr, es, pt, it, tr, th }

default.description: Required. The value the user gets

step.description: Step of the number field (arrow keys / wheel)

unit.description: mm for lengths (scale with the canvas), deg, count (whole numbers), none (ratios, strengths)

body.description: Required. Statements: {"let": {name: expr}}, {"for": "k", "from"?, "to", "step"?, "do": [...]}, {"if": expr, "then": [...], "else"?: [...]}, {"hole": {"x", "z" (or "r", "a"), "rotation"?, "size"?}} — rotation and size go INSIDE hole. Expressions are strings; trig in degrees. Full spec: get_pattern_schema("ai_custom") → custom_arrangement

values.description: Parameter values for this call only (e.g. to test the ends of a range); the defaults stay what the user gets

reference_image.description: Use an image as a controller: its brightness drives hole size / spacing / angle / shape across the canvas (the "reference image" workflow).

url.description: http(s) URL of a PNG or JPEG

path.description: Local file path (local MCP only; must be inside the folder the server was started in, its output folder, or a folder passed with --allow-dir)

data_base64.description: Raw PNG/JPEG bytes as base64 — only when your runtime hands you the real bytes (a file you read programmatically). Never retype a picture you can merely see: it will not decode. For a photo the user pasted into the chat, ask for a URL, or, if you have a code sandbox, call design_geometry and composite there.

preset.description: Use the background image stored in a marketplace preset, e.g. "#082" (get_recipe fills this in; keeps the recipe's imgScale / imgOffX / imgOffY)

mode.description: Which property the image brightness drives

invert.description: true = bright areas get the effect instead of dark

contrast.description: Gamma on the brightness map, 1 = as is

scale.description: mm per image pixel; default fits the image to the canvas

tools.name: export_design
tools.description: Generate the pattern and export files. Writes files to the local output folder and returns their paths. Like every SolidVents tool it needs a Pro account; exports also count against the hourly export quota. STEP (stp) is the 3D CAD format; SVG/DXF are 2D. ONLY call this when the user explicitly asks for a file, and export only the format(s) they asked for (one by default) — it is the expensive call. Otherwise finish with preview_design + open_in_app.

design.description: SolidVents design parameters: { pattern, ...keys from get_pattern_schema }. A full state from load_preset or an exported SVG also works.

svg.description: A SolidVents-exported SVG (its embedded state is used as the design; `design` keys override it).

gradients.description: Simplified gradient controllers; see get_pattern_schema → gradients. Appended to any controllers already in `design`.

fill.description: loop only. Default true = the whole interior is at target; false = only a band of radius on each side of the loop line (e.g. an outer ring of smaller holes)

curve.description: line/loop: smooth curve through the points instead of straight segments

corner_radius.description: line/loop without curve: round the corners (mm)

single_side.description: line/loop: affect only one side of the path

symmetric.description: angle: opposite angle on each side of the line

dropout.description: size: randomly remove this % of holes inside the range

repeat.description: Tile this controller across the whole canvas — for rhythms that repeat (clusters of big holes on a lattice, pulsing bands)

stagger.description: Shift every other row by dx/2

hole_shape.description: Custom hole outline as an SVG path. Use this for chevrons, slots, leaves, logos — anything beyond circle/rectangle/polygon/star. Sets pointShape to custom.

svg_path.description: SVG path data for one hole outline, e.g. "M0 0 L5 3 L10 0 L10 2.5 L5 5.5 L0 2.5 Z" (units arbitrary, y down). Use layers instead for composite holes.

circles.description: Construction outline (arcs + common tangent lines, the way logos are drawn): circles in order around the outline; r > 0 bulge, r < 0 dent, r = 0 corner. Units arbitrary, y down (same as svg_path). Rules and examples: CONSTRUCTION under hole_shape in get_pattern_schema.

r.description: Radius. r > 0: the outline bulges around this circle (convex arc, circle inside the shape); r < 0: the outline dents inward along it (concave arc, circle outside the shape); r = 0: a sharp corner at (x, y)

rect.description: A rectangle w × h centred on (0,0) instead of a path — bars, slats, strips. Place and turn it with transform. fillets rounds its corners

transform.description: Placement of this piece: turned by rotation about its own origin, then moved to (x, y); applied before mirror. Draw the piece around (0,0) and put its position here — no corner arithmetic for slanted bars

mirror.description: For the single outline given by svg_path / circles / rect; in layers each layer has its own. 2 = mirror across x = 0, 3–8 = copies turned about (0, 0); draw the shape once (open half or one repeat) — see SYMMETRY in get_pattern_schema.

layers.description: Composite hole: layers bottom→top with roles (union/subtract) and per-layer gradient behaviour, at most 12. See get_pattern_schema → hole_shape. If a unit needs more than 12 pieces, simplify the motif or make the unit smaller (a bigger repeat with fewer pieces per layer); say so to the user rather than silently dropping pieces.

gradient.description: Reaction to a size gradient: default scales with the hole, fixed never scales, independent scales about its own pivot

lock_width.description: independent layer: a size gradient does not change its width

lock_height.description: independent layer: a size gradient does not change its height

frame_rotation.description: independent layer: orientation (deg) of the box its pivot is taken from

fillets.description: Live rounded corners: a number rounds every sharp corner by that radius, or [{corner: anchor index, radius}] (same units as svg_path). Prefer this over drawing arcs by hand

lock_fillet.description: independent layer: corner radius stays the same when a size gradient scales the layer
